name: Guilin Liangjiang International Airport
before:
The airport for Guilin, about 28 km south west of the city, and the arrival point for one of China's most visited landscapes. It handled 6,504,366 passengers in 2025, 48th busiest in China, across 48 domestic and international destinations.

Terminal guidance needs checking. All flights moved from Terminal 1 to Terminal 2 on 30 September 2018, and Terminal 1 closed for renovation, so anything pointing a client at Terminal 1 is out of date.

Terminal 2 covers 100,000 square metres with 25 boarding gates and 22 security lanes, 17 domestic and 5 international, and was built for 12 million passengers a year. It cost 3.258 billion yuan.

The airport opened on 1 October 1996, replacing Guilin Qifengling Airport, and has a 3,200 metre runway.

claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The 2018 CARNOC report it cites came back as an empty script page (left alone, as in earlier batches), the operator's site did not answer, and Air China and Travel China Guide give none of these figures.
Wikipedia alone; Air China gives the 1996 opening but not what it replaced, and the operator's history page did not answer.
